site.title: gm
site.description: vibe coding ship fast, then claim work done. gm add checkable walk around coding agent. Walk = one run through gm state machine: 146 states (129 principles, disciplines subagent apply) joined by 376 edges. Gates on edge decide each move. Graph has 26 gate predicates: 24 block move, name failed condition; 2 only report. Pool of subagents work discipline graph parallel. One skill for Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Codex. Orchestrator, runs walk, written in rust, compiled to WebAssembly (wasm).

site.title: floosie
site.description: pipe anything to anything. the stream-composition primitive under streamtts and friends.

hero.heading: floosie
hero.body: 98 typed chunks, 14 operators, one composable runtime. the stream-composition primitive under streamtts and friends — written so you can fuse mime-detected stdin, websockets, ACP agents, and ML tensors into a single pipe() chain without writing glue.

flow.heading: anatomy of a pipeline
flow.intro: every floosie pipeline is the same shape. read top-to-bottom; the bytes flow the same way.
flow.ascii:
┌──────────────┐
│   source     │   stdin · ws · acp · file · iter
└──────┬───────┘
       ▼
┌──────────────┐
│ typed chunk  │   { type, data, meta:{mime} }
└──────┬───────┘   ◌ 98 variants · auto-detected
       ▼
┌──────────────┐
│  transform   │   .through(gate · parallel · scan · …)
└──────┬───────┘   ◌ 14 operators · sflow under the hood
       ▼
┌──────────────┐
│ processor    │   { name, status, chunksIn, chunksOut }
└──────┬───────┘   ◌ idle → running → error|stopped
       ▼
┌──────────────┐
│    sink      │   ndjson · ws · acp · file · iter
└──────────────┘

problem.heading: the pain you already know
problem.intro: every non-trivial stream pipeline drifts into the same swamp. floosie is the answer to a problem you've solved badly four times already.

items.name: untyped buffers
items.desc: Buffer<unknown> flowing between stages. is this json? a frame? a tensor header? you'll find out at runtime.

items.name: framing-by-hand
items.desc: newline-delimited here, length-prefixed there, websocket envelopes elsewhere. each new sink is a fresh parser.

items.name: no observability
items.desc: console.log scattered through transforms. no per-stage counters, no lifecycle, no introspection.

items.name: transport coupling
items.desc: rewriting a pipeline because you swapped stdio for a websocket. the logic was fine; the plumbing leaked.

when.heading: when to reach for floosie
when.intro: five shapes of problem where floosie pays for itself in the first hour.

items.name: agent pipelines
items.desc: an LLM emits tokens, your code routes by type — text vs tool-call vs error. ACP source/sink already wraps it.

items.name: media transforms
items.desc: image/video/audio/pdf flowing through detectors, encoders, sinks. file-type does the magic-byte work; you write the verbs.

items.name: ml inference fans
items.desc: tensors and embeddings as first-class chunks. parallel(fn, n) caps concurrency without juggling promises.

items.name: observability streams
items.desc: metrics, spans, logs, events as typed chunks. mux N sources, batch by time, route by category.

items.name: websocket fan-in/out
items.desc: muxWsClients() merges N upstreams into one chunk flow. wsBridge serves as a typed broadcast.

how.heading: how it actually works
how.intro: three primitives. you'll have the mental model in the time it takes to read this panel.

steps.name: chunk
steps.desc: every value in a flow is { type, data, meta }. the type is one of 98, the codec round-trips it, mime is auto-detected on binary.

steps.name: processor
steps.desc: createProcessor({ name, input, transform, output }) — the actor. transform is a sflow pipeline. lifecycle is idle/running/error/stopped, observed by the registry.

steps.name: operator
steps.desc: mux/split/gate/scan/zip/batch/window/throttle/debounce/parallel — each is a typed StreamNode. fuse with .through(). nothing else.

recipes.heading: recipes you can paste
recipes.intro: four real pipelines, each under 12 lines.

items.name: stdin → typed chunks → ndjson stdout
items.desc: the cli pipe. mime-sniffed, type-routed, framed for you.

items.name: fan N websockets into one stream
items.desc: muxWsClients with round-robin or hash routing.

items.name: concurrent classify with backpressure
items.desc: parallel caps concurrency, gate filters on score, withBackpressure protects upstream.

items.name: ACP agent as a stream source
items.desc: AgentClientProtocol → typed chunks. plug it into any operator chain.

items.name: you ship agent runtimes
items.desc: if streamtts, an LLM gateway, or any AgentClientProtocol consumer is on your roadmap, floosie is the layer you would have built.

items.name: you do byte-level work
items.desc: media transcoders, protocol bridges, telemetry routers. you spend more time on framing than logic. stop.

items.name: you want one mental model
items.desc: if you've written 'this is the third time i've reframed ndjson', the third time should be an import, not a parser.

proofs.heading: three things you get for free
proofs.intro: the boring stuff that ate your last sprint.

items.name: typed end-to-end
items.desc: every value carries its type at runtime. discriminated-union narrowing means no `as any` cast survives a code review.

items.name: mime detection
items.desc: binary in → file-type magic-byte lookup → mimeToChunkType() → variant selected. you wrote zero of those lines.

items.name: observed by default
items.desc: registry tracks every processor — chunksIn, chunksOut, errors, uptimeMs. setLogSink() forwards to your stack.

operators.heading: operators
operators.intro: all 14 are typed StreamNode factories. compose with pipe() / .through(). nothing else to learn.

items.name: mux(...sources)
items.desc: merge N async sources into one interleaved flow

items.name: split(flow, n)
items.desc: fan-out one stream into N independent branches

items.name: gate(pred)
items.desc: async predicate filter — keep only items that pass

items.name: scan(fn, seed)
items.desc: running accumulator — emit state after each item

items.name: zip(...sources)
items.desc: combine N sources into tuples, stop at shortest

items.name: withBackpressure(hwm)
items.desc: pause upstream when in-flight count exceeds HWM

items.name: batch(n)
items.desc: collect items into fixed-size arrays

items.name: window(ms)
items.desc: collect items into time-bounded arrays

items.name: throttle(ms)
items.desc: pass at most one item per interval

items.name: debounce(ms)
items.desc: suppress items until quiet for ms

items.name: take(n)
items.desc: emit first N items then close

items.name: drop(n)
items.desc: skip first N items

items.name: distinct(keyFn?)
items.desc: deduplicate consecutive equal items

items.name: parallel(fn, n)
items.desc: concurrent async map with concurrency limit

chunks.heading: the 98 chunk types
chunks.intro: every value in a floosie stream is a typed chunk with a codec, a mime hint, and a place in the discriminated union. 98 built-ins span media, text, network protocols, ML tensors, cryptographic primitives, and numeric scalars — and you can register your own.

usage.heading: the 8-line tour
usage.intro: one createProcessor, one transform, framing handled.

glossary.heading: vocab — the four words that matter
glossary.intro: if you know these, you know floosie.

items.def: { type, data, meta }. the atomic value in any flow. 98 built-in types; type narrows data.
encode/decode pair per chunk type. encodeChunk(c) → bytes, decodeChunk(type, bytes) → c. mime auto-populated on binary.
createProcessor({ name, input, transform, output }). the actor. lifecycle is idle → running → error | stopped.
a typed StreamNode factory you fuse with .through(). 14 of them. mux, gate, parallel, batch — that family.

items.name: cli flags

items.name: content-addressable cache
items.desc: BLAKE3-keyed embedding cache on disk; skips re-embedding unchanged chunks across runs.
